newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: WEAK PULA SAVES BOTSWANA MEAT COMMISSION FROM LOSS.
newsitem.headline: WEAK PULA SAVES BOTSWANA MEAT COMMISSION FROM LOSS.

text.p: The operations of the Botswana Meat Commission (BMC) recorded a reduced 10 million pula surplus for the year ended September 30, chairman Martin Mannathoko said on Monday.
This compares with 31.57 million pula in 1995 and 33.75 million pula in 1994.
Presenting unaudited preliminary results, Mannathoko said BMC had avoided recording a loss mainly because of the slide by the Botswana pula against all hard currrencies.
The pula is tied to the South Africa rand which has lost 20 per cent against the US dollar over the year to date.
Eighty percent of Botswana's beef is exported to Europe.
The results of operations in Europe, where the BMC owns cold stores and distribution companies were profitable, Mannathoko said.

"Trading over the year was very difficult. The mad cow disease in Europe resulted in panic by consumers and a significant drop in meat consumption and prices and Botswana experienced its own outbreak of cattle disease as the Ngamiland herd succumbed to cattle lung disease."
Throughput at BMC's abattoir at Maun slowed towards the end of the financial year because of the slaughter of 300,000 cattle as part of the effort to eradicate the disease in Ngamiland.
The abattoir was eventually forced to close.
Detailed results are not expected until March-April 1997.
